web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Platform — Revenue Streams, Geographies & Real Deployments
question: What does AvePoint actually sell across its four revenue lines and three product suites, and how do real enterprise and government customers deploy and pay for it?

epigraph.quote: As we tell enterprise leaders, your AI will find everything you forgot you had. Our promise is simple: move them from unmanaged AI to measurable trust.
epigraph.author: Dr. Tianyi Jiang (TJ), Q3 2026 Earnings Call

web_blocks.html: Under ASC 606 and SEC rules, AvePoint reports as one operating segment, but breaks revenue into four streams [1, 2]. Those streams are SaaS, Term License and Support, Services, and legacy Maintenance, which became immaterial and exited standalone reporting in 2026 [1, 2]. On a product basis, AvePoint groups its Confidence and Trust Platforms into three commercial suites [5, 27]. Resilience (~62% of ARR at year-end 2025) covers Cloud Backup, Rapid Recovery, and Opus records archiving [5, 27]. Control (~26% of ARR) spans Cloud Governance, Policies, Insights, tyGraph, EnPower, and AgentPulse [5, 27]. Modernization (~12% of ARR) houses Fly data migration and integration [5, 27]. Pricing is mainly a per-user, per-month subscription tied to total employee headcount or protected seats, plus storage tiers for heavy data estates [4, 21]. Fly migration is also quoted by data volume or user count [4, 21].

web_blocks.caption: AvePoint Revenue Mix by Stream & Geography (FY2023–9M 2026, $ Thousands)
web_blocks.takeaway: SaaS expanded from 59.2% of revenue in FY2023 to 80.5% in Q3 2026, while geographic exposure is unusually balanced across North America (39%), EMEA (33%), and APAC (28%).

web_blocks.html: 1. SaaS Revenue ($319.2M in FY2025; $297.4M in 9M 2026): Recognized ratably over annual or multi-year terms, SaaS drives the business [1, 2]. Concrete Example A (Public Sector): The County of Orange, California (15,000+ staff) needed to protect over 60 TB of Microsoft 365 data across Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams [22]. It also had to curb uncontrolled Teams sprawl [22]. Orange County deployed AvePoint Cloud Backup and AvePoint Cloud Governance through AvePoint Online Services [22]. Instead of writing PowerShell scripts to rebuild deleted Exchange mailboxes, IT restores full mailboxes with original folders in hours [22]. Cloud Governance enforces naming rules, agency cost tags, and inactivity archiving [22]. Concrete Example B (Multi-Cloud): Centerline, a Massachusetts critical-infrastructure firm with 1,375 employees, ran both Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 (180 TB combined) [25]. Centerline replaced its prior M365 vendor with AvePoint Cloud Backup across both clouds, cutting daily backup checks from 90 minutes to 10 minutes under one per-user subscription [25]. Concrete Example C (AI Agents): In Q3 2026, a major U.S. natural gas company (a customer since 2023) found ~3,000 unmanaged AI agents in its Microsoft 365 and Power Platform estate [4]. It upgraded to the Control Complete bundle, including AgentPulse, across ~7,000 users on a predictable per-employee fee [4].

2. Term License and Support ($41.4M in FY2025; $28.5M in 9M 2026): AvePoint sells bundled on-premises or hybrid licenses alongside support [1, 2]. The license portion books upfront on delivery, while support books ratably [1, 2]. This line shrinks by design (-7.1% in FY2025; -25.7% YoY in Q3 2026) as buyers shift to cloud SaaS [1, 2]. Still, it remains vital for air-gapped defense, sovereign, and hybrid sites [1, 2]. Concrete Example: Danish Crown, Europe's largest pork processor, protects 184+ TB of Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive data [23]. It completes 5 to 8 M&A integrations per year (10 to 400 users each) using AvePoint Cloud Backup and AvePoint Fly [23]. Fly's hybrid and SaaS connectors map user identities and delta-sync SharePoint sites [23]. That cuts migration cutover times by 50% and restores data 10–20x faster [23]. Likewise, federal contractor DTS (Arlington, VA) uses Fly under AvePoint's FedRAMP Moderate authorization [21]. DTS moves commercial Google, GoDaddy, and M365 tenants into Microsoft GCC High with 90% less migration labor [21].

3. Services ($53.8M in FY2025; $47.0M in 9M 2026): This bucket covers implementation, consulting, training, complex migrations, customization, and managed services [1, 2]. Revenue books on labor hours or straight-line over managed-service terms [1, 2]. Margins sit near breakeven—9M 2026 Services cost of $47.2M slightly topped $47.0M revenue—yet Services serves as a key enterprise wedge [2]. Concrete Example: A New Zealand public-service department (131 TB of M365 data) hired AvePoint and MSP partner Datacom [24]. Together they deployed AvePoint Opus (records lifecycle), AvePoint Insights (security posture), and Cloud Backup [24]. Advisory workshops trimmed 650+ legacy Archives New Zealand classification terms by 60% [24]. The team ran the agency's first defensible disposal of 5,000 obsolete records and revoked 11,000 of 14,000 external guest accounts [24]. Similarly, in Q3 2026, a top U.S. private research university (60,000 users) paired AvePoint software with AvePoint Managed Services [4]. The goal was to clean up overshared files across M365 and Google Workspace ahead of Copilot and Gemini rollouts [4].

4. Maintenance ($5.1M in FY2025; wound down in 2026): This stream captured legacy post-contract support (PCS) on old perpetual licenses and Technical Account Management (TAM) renewals [8, 9]. Once perpetual sales ended, maintenance fell from $29.1 million in FY2019 to $5.1 million in FY2025 [1, 9]. That completed AvePoint's multi-year exit from legacy on-premises maintenance [1, 9].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Notice that Services ($47.0M revenue vs. $47.2M cost in 9M 2026) runs basically at cost. That is a deliberate land-and-expand trade-off, not poor execution. A 60,000-user university or federal agency often lacks staff to fix 10 years of SharePoint permission sprawl before turning on Copilot. AvePoint's services team does that heavy lifting at breakeven so the 83%-gross-margin SaaS subscription sticks for a decade.

book_paragraphs: When you and I look inside AvePoint's 419.5 million dollars of FY2025 revenue and 372.8 million dollars in the first nine months of 2026, we see one platform sold across four accounting buckets. Soon there will be just three, because legacy Maintenance has finally wound down to irrelevance.

The growth engine is SaaS, which reached 80.5 percent of revenue in Q3 2026. Consider how real buyers use it. Orange County, California protects 60 terabytes of Microsoft 365 data across 15,000 staff. Its IT team uses Cloud Backup to restore full Exchange mailboxes in hours instead of writing PowerShell scripts, while Cloud Governance stops unowned Teams sprawl. Centerline in Massachusetts consolidated 180 terabytes of Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 onto Cloud Backup, cutting daily backup checks from 90 minutes to 10 minutes. In Q3 2026, a major U.S. gas utility found 3,000 rogue AI agents in its environment and upgraded 7,000 users to Control Complete with AgentPulse.

Second is Term License and Support, now under 7 percent of revenue and shrinking on purpose as customers move to the cloud. Still, it remains vital for hybrid, sovereign, or air-gapped sites. Danish Crown uses Cloud Backup and Fly to protect 184 terabytes and absorb five to eight acquisitions a year, cutting migration cutover times in half. Federal contractor DTS uses Fly's FedRAMP-authorized lane to move agencies into Microsoft GCC High with 90 percent less manual work.

Third is Services, at roughly 13 percent of revenue, where AvePoint runs implementations and managed services near breakeven. In New Zealand, AvePoint and partner Datacom helped a government agency cut 650 records classes by 60 percent with Opus and revoke 11,000 stale guest accounts flagged by Insights. Selling services at cost gets messy enterprise data AI-ready so the high-margin SaaS engine can compound.
